extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians in arithmetic geometry familiar with Inter-Universal Teichmüller (IUT) theory
extracted.subtask_description: Extraction of the conceptual/technical constraints and desiderata used in comparing the theta-theoretic and number-field parts of Mochizuki's IUT framework (multiradiality, Kummer theory choices, cyclotomic rigidity, compatibility with topologies/symmetries).

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment of multiradiality properties
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish multiradiality properties by using the geometric dimension of the elliptic curve as a 'multiradial geometric container' for the radial arithmetic data of interest (e.g., theta values 'q^{j^2}_v' or copies of the number field 'Fmod').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the theta case use the theory of theta functions on Tate curves to furnish such geometric containers; in the number-field case use the absolute anabelian interpretation of Belyi maps as cuspidalizations. Pass from these geometric containers to the radial arithmetic data by means of Galois evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Galois evaluation must be performed in the log-link context
rubrics_metrics.description: The associated Galois evaluation operations that give rise to theta values or copies of 'Fmod' are performed in the context of the log-link, which depends essentially on the arithmetic holomorphic (ring) structures of the local fields involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This dependence is crucial and ties into log-Kummer correspondences; constructions must respect these log-link contexts to produce the intended outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect label dependence and F_l-symmetries in the theta case
rubrics_metrics.description: In the theta case the output data (theta values) depends in an essential way on labels j ∈ F_l, and the cyclotomic rigidity construction must admit F_l^±-symmetries that are consistent with this label dependence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is a 'highly nontrivial fact' that the mono-theta-theoretic cyclotomic rigidity isomorphism admits F_l^±-symmetries; naive Kummer approaches fail to provide this.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid naive Kummer theory of algebraic rational functions
rubrics_metrics.description: The naive approach using algebraic rational functions (as in IUTchI Example 5.1(v)) is fundamentally incompatible with the profinite/tempered topology of the profinite fundamental groups involved and with other required symmetries/rigidities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on algebraic rational functions as multiradial containers in the local theory at v ∈ Vbad; instead use truncated Kummer theory of theta functions or Kummer theory of line bundles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use truncated Kummer theory of theta functions (mod N) for topology compatibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Truncated (mod N) Kummer theory of theta functions is compatible with the profinite/tempered topologies of the fundamental groups, unlike naive algebraic rational-function approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work with theta functions truncated modulo N to maintain compatibility with pro-finite/tempered topologies; however, naive truncated Kummer theory of theta functions may still fail other rigidity properties unless refined as below.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Kummer theory of first Chern classes / line bundles (not rational functions)
rubrics_metrics.description: To obtain compatibility with discrete rigidity and F_l^±-symmetry one must work with the Kummer theory of the first Chern classes of the line bundles associated to theta functions rather than with rational functions themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This amounts to considering the (partially truncated) arithmetic fundamental group of the G_m-torsor determined by such a line bundle, equipped appropriately with theta sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt mono-theta environments (theta sections but not algebraic sections)
rubrics_metrics.description: Working with mono-theta environments (i.e., equipped only with data corresponding to theta sections, not algebraic sections) is necessary to be compatible simultaneously with the tempered topology, F_l^±-symmetry, and the three types of rigidity considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text lists the incompatibilities: (i) neither theta nor algebraic sections ⇒ incompatible with constant multiple rigidity; (ii) bi-theta (both theta and algebraic) ⇒ incompatible with discrete rigidity and F_l^±-symmetry; (iii) algebraic sections only ⇒ incompatible with cyclotomic rigidity; only mono-theta yields compatibility with all desired properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat cyclotomic rigidity outputs up to indeterminacy (Iord) / be coric/invariant
rubrics_metrics.description: To avoid vicious circles/loops after identifying Frobenius-like and étale-like versions of objects, one must work with objects that are 'invariant' or 'coric' with respect to the indeterminacy submonoid Iord ⊆ ±N_{≥1} generated by the orders of zeroes/poles of the rational functions involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This indeterminacy is incompatible with constructions analogous to theta-value constructions when Iord is nontrivial. In theta cases Iord = {1} (orders =1 at cusps), avoiding the problem; in other cases one must account for Iord.

rubrics_metrics.name: In number-field case accept ±1 indeterminacy for outputs
rubrics_metrics.description: In the number-field case, after identifying μ_Fr with μ_∀^et one must regard the cyclotomic rigidity isomorphisms and their outputs (copies of F^×_mod, union {0}) as being subject to an indeterminacy constituted by possible multiplication by {±1}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This does not pose technical problems because the output data is stabilized by the action of {±1}; constructions should record and respect this ±1 indeterminacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure cyclotomic rigidity constructions are compatible with profinite/tempered topology
rubrics_metrics.description: Cyclotomic rigidity algorithms must be compatible with the topology of the profinite (or tempered) fundamental groups involved; approaches that depend on the discrete rigidity property Q_{>0}^× = {1} are incompatible with these topologies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Techniques that force discrete rigidity by using dense discrete subsets (e.g., reliance on N_{≥1} in Z_p context) conflict with the profinite topology and should be avoided or carefully modified (e.g., via EtTh-style constructions or truncated theta approaches).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use canonical uniformizers in mixed-characteristic local fields to avoid indeterminacy
rubrics_metrics.description: In mixed-characteristic local fields (MLF's), taking algebraic rational functions to be the uniformizers (one zero of order 1 and no poles) yields 'de facto' compatibility with the pro-finite/tempered topology and avoids indeterminacy issues because MLF's have a uniquely determined canonical valuation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is used in AbsTopIII-style constructions to obtain cyclotomic rigidity isomorphisms compatible with topology; view MLF/mono-theta as qualitative models for one-valuation/cusp cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve compatibility with the product formula (avoid independent indeterminacies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Independent indeterminacies (e.g., arising from Iord nontrivial acting independently at different places) are incompatible with the global product formula and with the structure of the global realiﬁed Frobenioids.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constructions must ensure any indeterminacy is globally controlled (e.g., trivial in theta case) so valuations at distinct v ∈ V remain consistent with the product formula.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prime-strip constructions via subquotient monoids O^⊥ and O^(5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given an F^(3)-prime-strip, at each w ∈ V_bad the splittings determine submonoids 'O^⊥(−) ⊆ O^(2)(−)' and quotient monoids 'O^⊥(−) (2) O^(5)(−)'; replace the split Frobenioid portions by the Frobenioids determined by these subquotient monoids to form F^(3)^⊥ and F^(3)^(5) collections, and similarly for F^(4)^⊥-prime-strips (satisfying the same conditions (a)–(f) as in IUTchI Def.5.2 but with the F^(3)-portion replaced).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives a precise procedural requirement for forming the modified prime-strips used in later multiradial/Galois-evaluation constructions; routine details are left to the reader but the replacement by sub/quotient monoids is mandatory for these variants.
